# dbd — Database Designer

> A standalone CLI and embeddable Rust library for managing database schemas as code.

dbd parses SQL DDL files, resolves dependencies, generates migrations, loads data, and deploys to PostgreSQL, Supabase, SQLite, or Convex — all from a single binary with zero runtime dependencies.

## Core concept

SQL files are the source of truth. File path determines the entity name:
- `ddl/table/config/lookups.ddl` → entity `config.lookups` (table)
- `ddl/view/config/genders.ddl` → entity `config.genders` (view)
- `ddl/procedure/staging/import_lookups.ddl` → entity `staging.import_lookups` (procedure)

Files are parsed once into a rich internal representation (Entity + TableDef). That same structure drives every feature: dependency graph, apply, migrations, DBML generation, data import.

## design.yaml structure

```yaml
project:
  name: MyProject

source:
  dialect: postgresql

target:
  postgres:
    url: $DATABASE_URL
    extensions: [uuid-ossp]
    roles:
      - name: app_user

schemas: [config, staging]

import:
  staging: [staging]
  options: { truncate: true, format: csv }

export:
  - config.lookups

dbml:
  base:
    exclude: { schemas: [staging] }
  core:
    include: { schemas: [config] }
    output: core.dbml          # filename (default: <key>.dbml)
    auto_group_by_schema: true # emit `TableGroup <schema>` per schema
    groups:                    # or explicit groups (precedence over auto)
      - name: lookups
        tables: [config.lookups, config.lookup_values]

scopes:                        # named entity subsets — deploy one design to many DBs
  hub:
    includes: [config, app.users]   # schema | schema.entity | schema.* (wildcard)
    deps: report               # report (default, errors on gaps) | include (auto-closure)
  reporting:
    excludes: [staging.*]      # wildcard drops a schema's entities but keeps the schema

ignore: [bfs, my_company.*]
```

Scopes are orthogonal to `target` (DB platform) and the connection: pair them at run time with `dbd deploy --scope hub --database $HUB_URL`. `includes`/`excludes` items are a bare schema (its entities + the schema entity), a qualified `schema.entity`, or a `schema.*` wildcard (same `prefix.*` syntax as `ignore:`; drops a schema's entities while keeping the schema — for `includes`, `schema.*` ≡ `schema`). A dependency gap (in-scope entity referencing a managed entity outside the scope) is an error under `report`; `external:` entities are never gaps. Omit `default`/the block ⇒ full set.

## Commands

- `dbd init` — scaffold project
- `dbd inspect` — validate, report errors/warnings (+ scope dependency gaps with `--scope`)
- `dbd apply` — apply schemas + entities + pending migrations
- `dbd import` — load staging data (CSV/TSV/JSONL)
- `dbd export` — export table data (scope-aware)
- `dbd deploy --source owner/repo/path` — fetch + apply + import from GitHub
- `dbd combine` — combine DDL into single SQL file (scope-aware)
- `dbd graph` — dependency graph as JSON (scope-aware)
- `dbd dbml` — generate DBML documentation (scope-aware: `--scope` filters to the scope's working set)
- `dbd snapshot` — capture schema version, generate migration SQL
- `dbd migrate` — apply pending migrations only
- `dbd doctor` — audit config for stale entries
- `dbd reset` — drop schemas (guarded by _dbd_meta env check; `--scope` restricts to the scope's schemas)
- `dbd format [--check]` — river-style DDL formatter; `--check` exits 1 if any file would change (drop-in for pre-commit; `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` ships `dbd-format` + `dbd-format-system`)

Global flags: `--scope <name>` selects a `scopes:` entity subset; `--deps report|include` overrides that scope's gap policy for one run. Honored by `inspect`/`apply`/`import`/`deploy` (gap-gated writes) and `dbml`/`combine`/`graph`/`export`/`reset` (filter-only — they don't gate on gaps; `inspect --scope` is where gaps surface). `reset` is schema-granular; the others filter to the entity working set.

## Architecture

- Parser: sqlparser-rs (pure Rust, multi-dialect)
- Adapters (all working):
    - PostgreSQL + Supabase (sqlx, `postgres://`) — COPY streaming import, namespace-aware catalog
    - SQLite (sqlx-sqlite, `sqlite://`/`sqlite::memory:`/`file:`) — batched multi-row INSERT (≤500 rows or 32k binds per batch), trigger-aware DDL splitter, ~150 builtins + `sqlite_*` prefix recognised offline
    - Convex (codegen, `convex:`/`convex://<dir>[?deploy=true]`) — flattens names, maps SQL → `v.*` validators, enums emit `export const X = v.union(v.literal(…))` above `defineSchema`, single-column FKs emit `v.id("table")`; opt-in `npx convex deploy` after apply; `import_data` shells out to `npx convex import` per table
- Classification: adapter-owned — each adapter knows its target's catalog (Postgres queries pg_proc/pg_type, SQLite uses a sorted builtins list + `sqlite_*` prefix rule, Convex defers everything to user-defined)
- Parallel parsing: rayon for CPU-bound file parse, tokio for async DB operations
- Library-first: `dbd-core` crate for embedding, `dbd-cli` for the binary
- Reference cache: `inspect --database` snapshots all user-defined entities to `.dbd/refcache.json`; subsequent offline runs consult it to silence "Unresolved reference" warnings without a live DB

## Key types

- `Entity` — central type for all DDL objects
- `TableDef` — parsed table structure (columns, FKs with actions, indexes, constraints, comments)
- `EntityType` — Schema, Extension, Role, Enum, Table, View, Function, Procedure, External, Import, Export
- `DatabaseAdapter` trait — connect, apply (single + batch), import/export, classify_reference, resolve_entity, list_entities, migration + meta tracking
- `RefCache` — JSON snapshot of remote entity names for offline `inspect`

## Safety

- `_dbd_meta` table records environment (dev/prod) and version in the database
- `dbd reset` blocked in prod (always) and in dev after v1 snapshot
- `--force` overrides safety guards
- For Convex (codegen target) the equivalent state lives in `<output>/.dbd_state.json`
